Appearance: A rat-sized mammal from rocks in Montana laid down within a few hundred thousand years of the asteroid impact that ended the age of dinosaurs, and one of the earliest undoubted placental mammals.

prompts.name: Darwinius
prompts.prompt: Darwinius (Darwinius masillae), a primate, about 58 cm long, in a lush emerald-green forest, Paleogene. Appearance: A lemur-like primate from the middle Eocene Messel pit in Germany, known from "Ida", an almost complete skeleton with fur outline and a last meal of fruit and leaves.

prompts.name: Aegyptopithecus
prompts.prompt: Aegyptopithecus (Aegyptopithecus zeuxis), a primate, about 60 cm long, in a lush emerald-green forest, Paleogene. Appearance: An early catarrhine primate from the early Oligocene of the Fayum in Egypt, close to the common ancestor of Old World monkeys and apes. About the size of a howler monkey, it climbed slowly through swampy tropical forest eating fruit.

prompts.name: Plesiadapis
prompts.prompt: Plesiadapis (Plesiadapis tricuspidens), a plesiadapiform, about 60 cm long, in a lush emerald-green forest, Paleogene. Appearance: A squirrel-like relative of the primates from the late Paleocene of Europe, about 60 cm long with a long bushy tail. It had claws instead of nails, eyes on the sides of its head and big gnawing front teeth like a rodent's.

prompts.name: Purgatorius
prompts.prompt: Purgatorius (Purgatorius unio), a plesiadapiform, about 15 cm long, in a lush emerald-green forest, Paleogene. Appearance: The earliest known plesiadapiform, the stem group of the primates, from the very beginning of the Paleocene of Montana, about 66 million years ago. Squirrel-sized, with a long tail, it is known from teeth, jaws and ankle bones;

prompts.name: Hoplophoneus
prompts.prompt: Hoplophoneus (Hoplophoneus primaevus), a nimravid, about 1.2 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Paleogene. Appearance: A leopard-sized "false sabre-tooth" of the early Oligocene of North America. Nimravids were cat-like carnivores that evolved long, flattened upper canines independently of the true sabre-toothed cats, sheathed by a bony flange on the lower jaw.

prompts.name: Miacis
prompts.prompt: Miacis (Miacis parvivorus), a miacid, about 30 cm long, in a lush emerald-green forest, Paleogene. Appearance: A small, tree-climbing meat-eater of the Eocene forests of North America, about 30 cm long plus a long bushy tail, built like a genet.

prompts.name: Daeodon
prompts.prompt: Daeodon (Daeodon shoshonensis), an entelodont, about 3.6 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Paleogene. Appearance: The largest entelodont or "hell pig", about 1.8 m tall at the shoulder, from the latest Oligocene and Early Miocene of North America. Its huge head had bony flanges under the cheeks and knobs under the chin, and its teeth could crack bones.

prompts.name: Deinotherium
prompts.prompt: Deinotherium (Deinotherium giganteum), a proboscidean, about 7 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: One of the largest land mammals ever, standing about 4 m at the shoulder, from the Middle and Late Miocene of Europe. Unlike elephants it had no upper tusks;

prompts.name: Platybelodon
prompts.prompt: Platybelodon (Platybelodon grangeri), a proboscidean, about 6 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: The "shovel-tusker", an elephant relative of the Middle Miocene of China, Mongolia and Kazakhstan, about 3 m tall. Its very long lower jaw ended in two broad, flat incisors forming a scoop, and a broad trunk rested on top of it.

prompts.name: Gomphotherium
prompts.prompt: Gomphotherium (Gomphotherium angustidens), a proboscidean, about 6 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A widespread elephant relative of the Middle Miocene of Europe, about 3 m at the shoulder. It had four tusks: two long upper tusks curving down and forward, and two shorter, straight lower tusks on a long lower jaw.

prompts.name: Chalicotherium
prompts.prompt: Chalicotherium (Chalicotherium grande), a chalicothere, about 3 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A strange relative of horses and rhinos from the Middle Miocene of Europe, about 2.6 m tall at the shoulder. Its long forelimbs and short hind legs gave it a gorilla-like sloping back, and it walked on its knuckles to keep its long hooked claws sharp.

prompts.name: Hipparion
prompts.prompt: Hipparion (Hipparion mediterraneum), an equid, about 1.7 m long, in a sunny savanna under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A pony-sized, three-toed horse of the Late Miocene of Greece and Turkey, known from rich fossil beds such as Pikermi and Samos.

prompts.name: Merychippus
prompts.prompt: Merychippus (Merychippus insignis), an equid, about 1.5 m long, in a wide grassy steppe under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: An early grazing horse of the Middle Miocene North American plains, about 1 m tall at the shoulder. It was one of the first horses with high-crowned teeth able to grind tough, gritty grass as grasslands spread.

prompts.name: Teleoceras
prompts.prompt: Teleoceras (Teleoceras major), a rhinocerotoid, about 4 m long, in a sunny savanna under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A hippo-like rhinoceros of the Miocene of North America, with a long barrel-shaped body, very short legs and a small horn on the tip of its nose.

prompts.name: Aepycamelus
prompts.prompt: Aepycamelus (Aepycamelus giraffinus), a camelid, about 3.3 m long, in a sunny savanna under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: The "giraffe camel" of the Middle and Late Miocene of North America, where camels first evolved. A humpless camel with very long, slender legs and a long neck, it held its small head about 3 m above the ground to browse on trees like a giraffe.

prompts.name: Giant Bear-dog
prompts.prompt: Giant Bear-dog (Amphicyon ingens), a bear dog, about 2.5 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: One of the largest "bear-dogs", from the Middle Miocene of North America, weighing perhaps 500 kg. Amphicyonids were carnivorans with a bear-like body, a wolf-like head and a long, heavy tail.

prompts.name: Sivapithecus
prompts.prompt: Sivapithecus (Sivapithecus indicus), a great ape, about 90 cm long, in a lush emerald-green forest, Neogene. Appearance: A chimpanzee-sized great ape of the Middle and Late Miocene of the Siwalik Hills of India and Pakistan, about 12.5 to 8.5 million years ago.

prompts.name: Lucy's Species
prompts.prompt: Lucy's Species (Australopithecus afarensis), a hominin, about 1.2 m long, in a sunny savanna under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: An early hominin of East Africa from about 3.9 to 2.9 million years ago, best known from the skeleton "Lucy" found in Ethiopia in 1974.

prompts.name: Ardipithecus
prompts.prompt: Ardipithecus (Ardipithecus ramidus), a hominin, about 1.2 m long, in a lush emerald-green forest, Neogene. Appearance: An early hominin that lived in woodland in Ethiopia about 4.4 million years ago, known from the partial skeleton "Ardi". It walked upright on the ground but kept an opposable big toe for grasping branches, a mix never seen in a living ape.

prompts.name: Sivatherium
prompts.prompt: Sivatherium (Sivatherium giganteum), a giraffid, about 4 m long, in a sunny savanna under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A massive okapi-like giraffid of the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene of the Indian subcontinent, weighing over a tonne, among the heaviest ruminants ever.

prompts.name: Samotherium
prompts.prompt: Samotherium (Samotherium boissieri), a giraffid, about 3.5 m long, in a sunny savanna under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A giraffid of the Late Miocene of Samos in Greece and Turkey, with a neck about half way in length between the okapi's and the giraffe's, and two long ossicones sweeping back above its eyes. Its neck bones show how the giraffe's long neck evolved in steps.

prompts.name: Thylacosmilus
prompts.prompt: Thylacosmilus (Thylacosmilus atrox), a sparassodont, about 1.6 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A jaguar-sized predator of the Late Miocene and Pliocene of Argentina, a sparassodont related to marsupials that evolved a sabre-toothed body like the cats on its own.

prompts.name: Phorusrhacos
prompts.prompt: Phorusrhacos (Phorusrhacos longissimus), a terror bird, about 2.5 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A flightless "terror bird" about 2.5 m tall from the Early and Middle Miocene of Patagonia, which gave the family Phorusrhacidae its name. It had long running legs, tiny wings and a huge head with a deep, hooked beak.

prompts.name: Kelenken
prompts.prompt: Kelenken (Kelenken guillermoi), a terror bird, about 3 m long, in a wide grassy steppe under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A terror bird of the Middle Miocene of Patagonia, about 15 million years ago, with the largest bird skull known: 71 cm long, most of it a narrow, hooked beak. Its long, slender lower legs suggest it was a fast runner despite standing about 3 m tall.

prompts.name: Argentavis
prompts.prompt: Argentavis (Argentavis magnificens), a teratorn, in flight, wings spread, about 2 m long, in a wide grassy steppe under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: One of the largest flying birds known, from the Late Miocene of Argentina, with a wingspan of about 6-7 m and a weight of some 70 kg.

prompts.name: Bony-toothed Bird
prompts.prompt: Bony-toothed Bird (Pelagornis chilensis), a pelagornithid, in flight, wings spread, about 1.5 m long, in a bright sunlit sea with vivid turquoise and cobalt blue water, Neogene. Appearance: A giant seabird of the Late Miocene of Chile with a wingspan of about 5.2 m, known from an unusually complete skeleton. Its long bill was lined with sharp, tooth-like spikes of bone (pseudo-teeth) for gripping fish and squid.

prompts.name: Livyatan
prompts.prompt: Livyatan (Livyatan melvillei), a toothed whale, about 15 m long, in a bright sunlit sea with vivid turquoise and cobalt blue water, Neogene. Appearance: A raptorial sperm whale of the Late Miocene of Peru, about 9 million years ago, perhaps 13-17 m long. Its teeth, up to 36 cm long in both jaws, are the largest of any animal used for eating, and it probably hunted baleen whales, competing with Megalodon.

prompts.name: Walrus Whale
prompts.prompt: Walrus Whale (Odobenocetops peruvianus), a toothed whale, about 3.5 m long, in a bright sunlit sea with vivid turquoise and cobalt blue water, Neogene. Appearance: A small whale related to narwhals from the Late Miocene and Pliocene of Peru that evolved a walrus-like face.

prompts.name: Aquatic Sloth
prompts.prompt: Aquatic Sloth (Thalassocnus natans), a ground sloth, about 2.5 m long, in a bright sunlit sea with vivid turquoise and cobalt blue water, Neogene. Appearance: A ground sloth of the Late Miocene coast of Peru that waded and swam into the sea to graze on seagrass and seaweed, because the land behind the coast was desert.

prompts.name: Purussaurus
prompts.prompt: Purussaurus (Purussaurus brasiliensis), a crocodilian, about 10.5 m long, in a clear river or lake with teal water and green plants, Neogene. Appearance: A giant caiman of the Late Miocene wetlands of the western Amazon, about 8 million years ago, probably 10-12 m long and weighing several tonnes, among the largest crocodylians ever.

prompts.name: Stupendemys
prompts.prompt: Stupendemys (Stupendemys geographicus), a side-necked turtle, about 3 m long, in a clear river or lake with teal water and green plants, Neogene. Appearance: A giant side-necked turtle of the Middle and Late Miocene rivers and lakes of northern South America, with a shell up to about 2.4-2.9 m long, one of the largest turtles ever. Males had two stout horns on the front of the shell, probably used in fights.

prompts.name: Megapiranha
prompts.prompt: Megapiranha (Megapiranha paranensis), a bony fish, about 80 cm long, in a clear river or lake with teal water and green plants, Neogene. Appearance: A giant relative of piranhas and pacus from the Late Miocene of Argentina, about 8-10 million years ago. Known only from part of a jaw, it had a zig-zag row of teeth halfway between the double row of pacus and the single row of piranhas.

prompts.name: Desmostylus
prompts.prompt: Desmostylus (Desmostylus hesperus), a desmostylian, about 2.8 m long, in a bright sunlit sea with vivid turquoise and cobalt blue water, Neogene. Appearance: A hippo-like marine mammal of the Middle Miocene coasts of the North Pacific, from Japan to California. Desmostylians are the only order of marine mammals that has completely died out; its name means "bundle of pillars", from the shape of its molar teeth.

prompts.name: Dinocrocuta
prompts.prompt: Dinocrocuta (Dinocrocuta gigantea), a percrocutid, about 2 m long, in a sunny savanna under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A lion-sized bone-cracking carnivore of the Late Miocene of Eurasia and Africa, a percrocutid, related to hyenas and cats rather than a true hyena. It had a massive head with a short muzzle and powerful jaws able to crush bones.

prompts.name: Horned Gopher
prompts.prompt: Horned Gopher (Ceratogaulus hatcheri), a rodent, about 30 cm long, in a wide grassy steppe under a blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A burrowing rodent about 30 cm long from the Late Miocene and Early Pliocene of the North American Great Plains, the smallest mammal known to have had horns. A pair of bony horns rose from its nose, perhaps for defence or display rather than digging.

prompts.name: Giant Moonrat
prompts.prompt: Giant Moonrat (Deinogalerix koenigswaldi), a gymnure, about 60 cm long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Neogene. Appearance: A giant gymnure, a hairy relative of hedgehogs, from the Late Miocene island of Gargano in Italy. It grew to about the size of a cat, with a long, cone-shaped snout, coarse fur instead of spines and a long naked tail.

prompts.name: Siberian Unicorn
prompts.prompt: Siberian Unicorn (Elasmotherium sibiricum), a rhinocerotoid, about 5 m long, in a wide grassy steppe under a blue sky, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: A giant rhinoceros of the Pleistocene steppes from the Black Sea to Kazakhstan and Mongolia, about 2 m tall and weighing up to 4 tonnes. A huge bony dome on its forehead is thought to have carried a single long horn.

prompts.name: Woolly Rhinoceros
prompts.prompt: Woolly Rhinoceros (Coelodonta antiquitatis), a rhinocerotoid, about 3.8 m long, in a wide grassy steppe under a blue sky, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: A rhinoceros of the Ice Age mammoth steppe of northern Eurasia, covered in long, thick hair and with small ears and a short tail to save heat.

prompts.name: Irish Elk
prompts.prompt: Irish Elk (Megaloceros giganteus), a deer, about 3 m long, in a wide grassy steppe under a blue sky, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: A giant deer of Pleistocene Eurasia, standing about 2 m at the shoulder, whose males grew the largest antlers of any deer, up to 3.6 m across and 40 kg, shed and regrown each year.

prompts.name: Diprotodon
prompts.prompt: Diprotodon (Diprotodon optatum), a marsupial, about 3.3 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: The largest marsupial that ever lived, a wombat relative the size of a hippopotamus, weighing up to 2.7 tonnes. It roamed the open woodlands and grasslands of Pleistocene Australia, and fossils suggest it migrated with the seasons.

prompts.name: Marsupial Lion
prompts.prompt: Marsupial Lion (Thylacoleo carnifex), a marsupial, about 1.5 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: A leopard-sized marsupial predator of Pleistocene Australia, related to wombats and koalas. Pound for pound it had one of the strongest bites of any mammal, with blade-like cheek teeth instead of long canines, and a huge claw on each thumb.

prompts.name: Glyptodon
prompts.prompt: Glyptodon (Glyptodon clavipes), a glyptodont, about 3.3 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: A car-sized armadillo relative of Pleistocene South America, weighing up to 2 tonnes. Its domed shell, about 1.5 m tall, was made of over a thousand fused bony plates, and it had a bony cap on its head and a tail armoured with rings of plates.

prompts.name: South Island Giant Moa
prompts.prompt: South Island Giant Moa (Dinornis robustus), a moa, about 3 m long, in a lush emerald-green forest, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: The tallest bird ever known, from New Zealand's South Island: females could reach 3.6 m with the neck raised and weighed up to 250 kg, far more than the males.

prompts.name: Giant Short-faced Bear
prompts.prompt: Giant Short-faced Bear (Arctodus simus), a bear, about 3 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: One of the largest carnivorous land mammals, a bear of Pleistocene North America that stood about 1.6 m at the shoulder on all fours and weighed up to 900 kg.

prompts.name: Macrauchenia
prompts.prompt: Macrauchenia (Macrauchenia patachonica), a litoptern, about 3 m long, in open green plains under a crisp blue sky, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: A camel-like hoofed mammal of Pleistocene South America with a long neck, three-toed feet and nostrils high on its head, often shown with a short trunk. Charles Darwin found its bones in 1834 and thought it was a giant llama.

prompts.name: Toxodon
prompts.prompt: Toxodon (Toxodon platensis), a notoungulate, about 2.7 m long, in a sunny savanna under a blue sky, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: A rhinoceros-sized hoofed mammal of Pleistocene South America, with a barrel body, short legs and a broad head with ever-growing teeth. Darwin collected its skull in Uruguay during the voyage of the Beagle.

prompts.name: Neanderthal
prompts.prompt: Neanderthal (Homo neanderthalensis), a hominin, about 1.65 m long, in a wide grassy steppe under a blue sky, Pleistocene-to-present. Appearance: Our closest extinct relatives, who lived in Europe and western Asia from about 400,000 to 40,000 years ago.
